questions.prompt: How can a scheduled task be hidden from schtasks /query and the Task Scheduler GUI while still running?
options: By setting its start type to disabled
By deleting the SD (security descriptor) value under TaskCache\Tasks\{GUID} in the registry
questions.explanation: Removing the security descriptor value hides the task from enumeration tools while the scheduler continues to execute it -- so a task present in the XML directory or registry but absent from schtasks output is deliberately hidden.

questions.prompt: Which scheduled task registration event is most reliably available during an investigation?
options: Security 4698, because it is always enabled
TaskScheduler/Operational 106, because that log is on by default while 4698 depends on audit policy
questions.explanation: Security log event 4698 requires 'Audit Other Object Access Events' to be enabled, which frequently is not. The Operational log is enabled by default, making 106 the more dependable record.

questions.prompt: Where do scheduled task XML definitions live on disk?
options: The registry only; there are no files
questions.explanation: Task definitions are stored as extensionless XML files under C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\, with subfolders mirroring the Task Scheduler tree.

questions.prompt: Why is a task located in the root \ folder more suspicious than one under \Microsoft\Windows\?
options: Root-folder tasks cannot run as SYSTEM
Legitimate installers rarely place tasks in the root folder, while attackers routinely do
The root folder does not exist by default
questions.explanation: Well-behaved software places its tasks in a Microsoft or vendor-named subfolder. A task sitting directly in the root is an outlier worth explaining.
